records.source: Τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ γεννηθέντος ἐν Βηθλέεμ τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἐν ἡμέραις Ἡρῴδου τοῦ βασιλέως, ἰδοὺ μάγοι ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν παρεγένοντο εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα λέγοντες· Ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ τεχθεὶς βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων;
records.gloss: The then Jesus having been born in Bethlehem of the Judea in days of Herod the king, behold, magi from risings arrived into Jerusalem \v 2 saying, Where is the [one] having been born king of the Jews?
pieces: When Jesus had been born in Bethlehem of Judea, in the days of King Herod, magi from the east arrived in Jerusalem
with a question: "Where is the newborn king of the Jews?

L.1: Now when Jesus had been born in Bethlehem of Judea in [the] days of Herod the king, look, magi from [the] east arrived in Jerusalem,
L.2: saying, "Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews?

R.1: Jesus was born in the town of Bethlehem in Judea, at the time when Herod was king. After that, some wise men who studied the stars came from the east to Jerusalem.
R.2: They asked, "Where is the child who has been born to be king of the Jews?

decisions.choice: magi: learned men from the east who studied the stars and interpreted signs and dreams
decisions.reason: The word first named a class of Persian priests, and came to be used for experts in the stars and in dreams in Persia and Babylon (compare Daniel 2:2, 48 in the Greek Old Testament). Matthew does not say they were kings or how many there were; the number three comes from the three gifts (2:11).

decisions.choice: Herod the king: Herod the Great, king of Judea under Rome, who died in 4 BC
decisions.reason: Rome made Herod king of the Jews, and he ruled from 37 to 4 BC. Jesus was born, then, before 4 BC. A child born "king of the Jews" (2:2) is a rival to the man who holds that title.

decisions.choice: Bethlehem of Judea: David's town, a few miles south of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: There was also a Bethlehem in Galilee (Joshua 19:15). Matthew names the one in Judea, the town of David (1 Samuel 16:1), as the prophecy in 2:6 will.

decisions.choice: the one born king: a king by birth, not one who has taken the throne
alternatives: one who will later be made king
decisions.reason: The magi do not ask for a future king but for one born as king of the Jews. Matthew uses the title again only at Jesus's trial and death (27:11, 29, 37).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this word to point to what comes next. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal uses "look", and Balanced and Readable carry its force in the flow of the sentence, as in 1:20.

decisions.choice: wise men
decisions.reason: "Magi" is unfamiliar to new readers; Readable calls them wise men, and in 2:1 says that they studied the stars.

decisions.choice: the child who has been born to be king
decisions.reason: Readable names the one they are looking for as a child and says what "born king" means.

records.heading: The magi visit the child

records.source: εἴδομεν γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὸν ἀστέρα ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ καὶ ἤλθομεν προσκυνῆσαι αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: We saw for of him the star in the rising, and we came to worship him.
pieces: We saw {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} star when it rose, and we have come to worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

L.2: For we saw {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} star at [its] rising and have come to worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

R.2: We saw {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} star rise in the sky, and we have come to worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: at its rising: when the star first appeared in the sky
alternatives: in the east, where the magi were
decisions.reason: In 2:1 "from the east" is plural and has no article. Here the word is singular with the article, as astronomers used it for a star's rising. The star's rising fits Herod's question about when it appeared (2:7).

decisions.choice: worship: bow down before him in honor
alternatives: pay homage, the honor given to a king, with no sense of worship
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow low before someone, to a king as well as to God. The magi come to honor a newborn king; in Matthew the same verb is used when the disciples worship Jesus (14:33; 28:9, 17), so Matthew's readers hear more in it than the magi may have meant. "Worship" keeps both senses in view.

decisions.choice: his star: a star that marks his birth; perhaps an echo of Numbers 24:17
alternatives: a star that belongs to him in some other sense
decisions.reason: People of the time believed a star could announce the birth of a great ruler. Balaam's prophecy speaks of "a star" that will come out of Jacob and a ruler from Israel (Numbers 24:17), and Balaam too was a seer from the east. Matthew does not quote the passage.

decisions.choice: "for" not rendered
decisions.reason: The Greek "for" gives the reason for their question. In English a new sentence makes the link without it.

records.source: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἡρῴδης ἐταράχθη καὶ πᾶσα Ἱεροσόλυμα μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ συναγαγὼν πάντας τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ γραμματεῖς τοῦ λαοῦ ἐπυνθάνετο παρ’ αὐτῶν ποῦ ὁ χριστὸς γεννᾶται.
records.gloss: Having heard then the king Herod was troubled and all Jerusalem with him, \v 4 and having gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people he was inquiring from them where the Christ is born.
pieces: When King Herod heard this, he was shaken, and so was all Jerusalem.
He called together all the chief priests and the scribes of the people and asked them where the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} was to be born.

L.3: And when King Herod heard [this], he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him,
L.4: and gathering all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired of them where the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} is to be born.

R.3: King Herod was upset when he heard this, and so were all the people in Jerusalem.
R.4: He called together all the leading priests and the teachers of God's law. He asked them where the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} would be born.

decisions.choice: troubled: alarmed, Herod at a rival and Jerusalem at what might follow
decisions.reason: The verb means stirred up, thrown into fear. Herod guarded his throne jealously. The city had reason to fear what he would do, and the turmoil a new king might bring.

decisions.choice: the chief priests and scribes: the leaders of the temple and the experts in the Scriptures
alternatives: the council as a formal court
decisions.reason: The chief priests were the high priest and the leading priestly families. The scribes studied, copied and taught the law of Moses. Herod asks them because they know the Scriptures.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, the king Israel was waiting for
decisions.reason: Herod hears "king of the Jews" and asks about "the Christ". He takes the newborn king to be the promised Messiah.

decisions.choice: is born: where the Messiah is to be born, by what Scripture says
alternatives: where he has just been born
decisions.reason: The present tense asks where, by the prophets, the Messiah's birth belongs. The answer in 2:5-6 is a passage of Scripture.

decisions.choice: teachers of God's law (R); scribes (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Scribes" today suggests people who only copy. Readable says what they did.

decisions.choice: heard [this]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the object English needs.

records.source: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἐν Βηθλέεμ τῆς Ἰουδαίας· οὕτως γὰρ γέγραπται διὰ τοῦ προφήτου·
records.gloss: They then said to him, In Bethlehem of the Judea; thus for it has been written through the prophet:
pieces: "In Bethlehem in Judea," they told him, "because this is what the prophet wrote:

L.5: And they said to him, "In Bethlehem of Judea, for so it has been written through the prophet:

R.5: They told him, "In Bethlehem in Judea. That is what the prophet Micah wrote:

decisions.choice: it has been written: it stands written, and still holds
decisions.reason: The perfect tense speaks of Scripture as a word that was written and still stands.

decisions.choice: the prophet: Micah, whose words are quoted in 2:6
decisions.reason: The words in 2:6 come mostly from Micah 5:2, with the last line from 2 Samuel 5:2.

decisions.choice: the prophet Micah
decisions.reason: Readable names the prophet.

records.source: Καὶ σύ, Βηθλέεμ γῆ Ἰούδα, οὐδαμῶς ἐλαχίστη εἶ ἐν τοῖς ἡγεμόσιν Ἰούδα· ἐκ σοῦ γὰρ ἐξελεύσεται ἡγούμενος, ὅστις ποιμανεῖ τὸν λαόν μου τὸν Ἰσραήλ.
records.gloss: And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, by no means least are among the rulers of Judah; out of you for will come forth [one] ruling, who will shepherd the people of me the Israel.
pieces: 'And you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are far from the least among the leading towns of Judah, for from you will come a leader who will be the shepherd of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'"

L.6: 'And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, in no way are [you] least among the rulers of Judah, for from you will go out a leader who will shepherd {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'"

R.6: 'Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, you are not the least important of the towns of Judah. A leader will come from you. He will care for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel as a shepherd cares for sheep.'"

decisions.choice: Micah 5:2 joined to 2 Samuel 5:2
decisions.reason: The first lines are from Micah 5:2, which promises a ruler from Bethlehem, David's town. The last line, "who will shepherd my people Israel", is what God said to David (2 Samuel 5:2). Together they say the promised ruler is a new David.

decisions.choice: by no means least: Bethlehem is no longer small, because of the ruler born there
alternatives: a mistake for Micah's "small among the clans of Judah"
decisions.reason: Micah calls Bethlehem small among Judah's clans. Matthew's wording turns this around: the birth of this ruler has made the small town great.

decisions.choice: the rulers of Judah: the leading towns of Judah, named by their rulers
alternatives: the governors of Judah as persons
decisions.reason: Bethlehem is compared with others like it. Micah speaks of Judah's clans; here the word for rulers stands for the chief places those rulers led.

decisions.choice: shepherd: rule and care for, as a shepherd leads a flock
decisions.reason: In Scripture the shepherd is a picture of a king who protects and feeds his people (2 Samuel 5:2; Ezekiel 34:23). The speaker who calls Israel "my people" is God.

decisions.choice: the leading towns (B); the towns (R)
decisions.reason: "Least among the rulers" would sound as if Bethlehem were a person. Balanced and Readable say what is being compared.

decisions.choice: care for my people as a shepherd cares for sheep
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture.

records.source: Τότε Ἡρῴδης λάθρᾳ καλέσας τοὺς μάγους ἠκρίβωσεν παρ’ αὐτῶν τὸν χρόνον τοῦ φαινομένου ἀστέρος, καὶ πέμψας αὐτοὺς εἰς Βηθλέεμ εἶπεν· Πορευθέντες ἐξετάσατε ἀκριβῶς περὶ τοῦ παιδίου· ἐπὰν δὲ εὕρητε, ἀπαγγείλατέ μοι, ὅπως κἀγὼ ἐλθὼν προσκυνήσω αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: Then Herod secretly having called the magi ascertained from them the time of the appearing star, \v 8 and having sent them to Bethlehem he said, Having gone search carefully concerning the child; when then you find, report to me, so that I also having come may worship him.
pieces: Herod then summoned the magi in private and questioned them to learn the exact time the star had appeared.

He sent them on to Bethlehem with these words: "Go and find out all you can about the child. When you have found {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, send word back to me, so that I may come and worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as well."

L.7: Then Herod, having secretly called the magi, learned exactly from them the time of the star's appearing,
L.8: and sending them to Bethlehem, he said, "Go and search carefully for the child, and when you have found [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], report to me, so that I too may come and worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

R.7: So Herod called the wise men to a secret meeting. He asked them exactly when the star had first appeared.
R.8: Then he sent them to Bethlehem. He told them, "Go and look carefully for the child. When you find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, come back and tell me. Then I can go and worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} too."

decisions.choice: secretly: Herod hides his purpose from the city and its leaders
decisions.reason: He meets the magi apart from the priests and scribes. The secrecy belongs to the plan Matthew reveals in 2:13 and 2:16.

decisions.choice: the time of the star's appearing: when it first appeared
decisions.reason: Herod wants to know how old the child might be. He uses the answer in 2:16.

decisions.choice: so that I too may worship him: a false reason that hides Herod's intent
decisions.reason: The angel's warning shows that Herod means to kill the child (2:13), and his slaughter of the boys of Bethlehem confirms it (2:16).

decisions.choice: wise men
decisions.reason: "Magi" is unfamiliar to new readers; Readable calls them wise men, and in 2:1 says that they studied the stars.

decisions.choice: found [him]
decisions.reason: Greek can leave the object of "find" unspoken; English needs it.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες τοῦ βασιλέως ἐπορεύθησαν, καὶ ἰδοὺ ὁ ἀστὴρ ὃν εἶδον ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ προῆγεν αὐτούς, ἕως ἐλθὼν ἐστάθη ἐπάνω οὗ ἦν τὸ παιδίον.
records.gloss: They then having heard the king went, and behold, the star which they saw in the rising went before them until having come it stood over where was the child.
pieces: They listened to the king and set out. And there was the star they had seen at its rising, going ahead of them, until it came and stood over the place where the child was.

L.9: And having heard the king, they went, and look, the star that they had seen at [its] rising went ahead of them until it came and stood over [the place] where the child was.

R.9: After they heard what the king said, they left. The star they had seen rising in the sky went ahead of them. It stopped over the place where the child was.

decisions.choice: at its rising: when the star first appeared in the sky
alternatives: in the east, where the magi were
decisions.reason: In 2:1 "from the east" is plural and has no article. Here the word is singular with the article, as astronomers used it for a star's rising. The star's rising fits Herod's question about when it appeared (2:7).

decisions.choice: the star went ahead and stood over the place: God guiding the magi to the child
alternatives: an ordinary movement of a star or planet
decisions.reason: Matthew tells it as guidance, not as an event in the sky that can be explained. The star leads them, then stops over one place.

decisions.choice: look (L); there was (B); not rendered (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this word to point to what comes next. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal uses "look", and Balanced and Readable carry its force in the flow of the sentence, as in 1:20.

records.source: ἰδόντες δὲ τὸν ἀστέρα ἐχάρησαν χαρὰν μεγάλην σφόδρα.
records.gloss: Having seen then the star they rejoiced joy great exceedingly.
pieces: The sight of the star filled them with a very great joy.

L.10: And seeing the star, they rejoiced [with] exceedingly great joy.

R.10: When they saw the star, they were filled with joy, more joy than they had ever known.

decisions.choice: rejoiced with exceedingly great joy: the strongest way Greek can say it
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun share one root, and two more words strengthen them: "they rejoiced a joy great exceedingly". The star stopping over the place (2:9) showed them they had arrived.

decisions.choice: filled them with a very great joy (B); more joy than they had ever known (R)
decisions.reason: English cannot pile up the words the way Greek does. Balanced keeps "joy" with two strengtheners; Readable states the degree plainly.

records.source: καὶ ἐλθόντες εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν εἶδον τὸ παιδίον μετὰ Μαρίας τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ πεσόντες προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἀνοίξαντες τοὺς θησαυροὺς αὐτῶν προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ δῶρα, χρυσὸν καὶ λίβανον καὶ σμύρναν.
records.gloss: And having come into the house they saw the child with Mary the mother of him, and having fallen they worshiped him, and having opened the treasures of them they offered to him gifts, gold and frankincense and myrrh.
pieces: Entering the house, they found the child with Mary {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother. They fell to the ground and worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they opened their chests of treasure and offered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} gifts: gold, frankincense and myrrh.

L.11: And coming into the house they saw the child with Mary {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother, and falling down they worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and opening their treasure chests they offered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} gifts, gold and frankincense and myrrh.

R.11: They went into the house and saw the child with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother Mary. They bowed down to the ground and worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then they opened the boxes that held their treasures and gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} gifts. They gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} gold, and frankincense and myrrh, costly spices with a sweet smell.

decisions.choice: fell down and worshiped him: bowed to the ground before him in honor
alternatives: pay homage, the honor given to a king, with no sense of worship
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow low before someone, to a king as well as to God. The magi come to honor a newborn king; in Matthew the same verb is used when the disciples worship Jesus (14:33; 28:9, 17), so Matthew's readers hear more in it than the magi may have meant. "Worship" keeps both senses in view.

decisions.choice: gold, frankincense and myrrh: costly gifts fit for a king
alternatives: gifts with a hidden meaning for each
decisions.reason: Frankincense is a resin burned for its scent, and myrrh a resin used in perfume, medicine and burial. Both came from Arabia and East Africa. Psalm 72:10-15 and Isaiah 60:6 picture nations bringing gold and incense to Israel's king. Matthew does not give each gift a meaning.

decisions.choice: the house: the family's home in Bethlehem, some time after the birth
decisions.reason: Matthew speaks of a house and a child, not a newborn. Herod's order in 2:16 for boys of two and under suggests that some months may have passed.

decisions.choice: costly spices with a sweet smell
decisions.reason: Readable says what these two gifts were.

decisions.choice: treasure chests (L); chests of treasure (B); the boxes that held their treasures (R)
decisions.reason: The word means a treasure or the box it is kept in. Since they "opened" them, boxes are meant.

records.source: καὶ χρηματισθέντες κατ’ ὄναρ μὴ ἀνακάμψαι πρὸς Ἡρῴδην δι’ ἄλλης ὁδοῦ ἀνεχώρησαν εἰς τὴν χώραν αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And having been warned in a dream not to return to Herod, by another way they withdrew into the country of them.
pieces: And since they had been warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, they went home to their own country by a different road.

L.12: And having been warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they withdrew to their own country by another way.

R.12: God warned them in a dream not to go back to Herod. So they went home to their own country by another road.

decisions.choice: warned: given a warning by God
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a message from God (2:22; Hebrews 8:5; 11:7). Matthew does not name the speaker, but the warning is God's.

decisions.choice: withdrew: left to get away from danger
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this verb for moving away from a threat (2:13, 14, 22; 4:12; 12:15).

decisions.choice: God warned them
decisions.reason: Readable names God, which the passive implies.

records.source: Ἀναχωρησάντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος κυρίου φαίνεται κατ’ ὄναρ τῷ Ἰωσὴφ λέγων· Ἐγερθεὶς παράλαβε τὸ παιδίον καὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ φεῦγε εἰς Αἴγυπτον, καὶ ἴσθι ἐκεῖ ἕως ἂν εἴπω σοι· μέλλει γὰρ Ἡρῴδης ζητεῖν τὸ παιδίον τοῦ ἀπολέσαι αὐτό.
records.gloss: Having withdrawn then of them, behold, an angel of Lord appears in a dream to the Joseph saying, Having arisen take the child and the mother of him and flee into Egypt, and be there until I tell you; is about for Herod to seek the child to destroy him.
pieces: When the magi had gone, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream and told him, "Get up and flee to Egypt with the child and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother. Remain there until I give you word, for Herod means to hunt for the child and destroy {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

L.13: And when they had withdrawn, look, an angel of [the] Lord appears in a dream to Joseph, saying, "Get up, take the child and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother and flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, for Herod is about to search for the child to destroy {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

R.13: After the wise men left, an angel of the Lord came to Joseph in a dream. The angel said, "Get up! Take the child and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother and run away to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you to leave. Herod is going to look for the child so that he can kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: Egypt: beyond Herod's rule, with large Jewish communities
alternatives: a place chosen for no reason
decisions.reason: Egypt was a Roman province outside Herod's kingdom, a few days' journey away, and many Jews lived there, above all in Alexandria. It had long been a refuge (1 Kings 11:40; Jeremiah 26:21).

decisions.choice: Herod seeking to destroy the child: an echo of Pharaoh and Moses
decisions.reason: Pharaoh ordered Hebrew boys killed (Exodus 1:22) and sought to kill Moses (Exodus 2:15). In 2:16 and 2:20 Matthew tells Jesus's story in words that recall Moses's.

decisions.choice: the child and his mother: Joseph is not called the child's father
decisions.reason: Throughout chapter 2 Matthew says "the child and his mother" (2:13, 14, 20, 21), in keeping with 1:18-25.

decisions.choice: appears (L); appeared (B, R)
decisions.reason: Greek often tells a past event in the present tense for vividness. Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past, as English narrative does.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this word to point to what comes next. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal uses "look", and Balanced and Readable carry its force in the flow of the sentence, as in 1:20.

records.heading: The escape to Egypt

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἐγερθεὶς παρέλαβε τὸ παιδίον καὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ νυκτὸς καὶ ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς Αἴγυπτον, καὶ ἦν ἐκεῖ ἕως τῆς τελευτῆς Ἡρῴδου· ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑπὸ κυρίου διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Ἐξ Αἰγύπτου ἐκάλεσα τὸν υἱόν μου.
records.gloss: He then having arisen took the child and the mother of him by night and withdrew into Egypt, \v 15 and was there until the death of Herod; so that may be fulfilled the [thing] spoken by Lord through the prophet saying, Out of Egypt I called the son of me.
pieces: Joseph got up, took the child and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother while it was still night, and left for Egypt.
He stayed there until Herod died, so that the word the Lord had spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled: "Out of Egypt I called {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son."

L.14: So he got up and took the child and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother by night and withdrew to Egypt,
L.15: and he was there until the death of Herod, so that what was spoken by [the] Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, "Out of Egypt I called {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son."

R.14: So Joseph got up. He left for Egypt during the night with the child and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother.
R.15: They stayed there until Herod died. This made what the Lord had said through the prophet Hosea come true: "I called {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son out of Egypt."

decisions.choice: Hosea 11:1: God's son Israel, called out of Egypt, and now Jesus
alternatives: a prediction about the Messiah only
decisions.reason: In Hosea the son is Israel, whom God brought out of Egypt in the exodus. Matthew sees Jesus, God's Son, going through Israel's story again: into Egypt and out of it. God calls Jesus "my Son" in 3:17.

decisions.choice: the quotation follows the stay in Egypt, not the return
decisions.reason: Matthew quotes the verse about leaving Egypt when the family arrives there. Their stay is what makes the coming out possible, which 2:19-21 then tells.

decisions.choice: got up and took: he does at once what he was told
alternatives: he made plans to leave later
decisions.reason: The words repeat the angel's command (2:13), as in 1:24 and 2:21. "By night" adds that he did not wait for morning.

decisions.choice: Joseph
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Joseph at the start of the sentence.

decisions.choice: the prophet Hosea
decisions.reason: Readable names the prophet.

records.source: Τότε Ἡρῴδης ἰδὼν ὅτι ἐνεπαίχθη ὑπὸ τῶν μάγων ἐθυμώθη λίαν, καὶ ἀποστείλας ἀνεῖλεν πάντας τοὺς παῖδας τοὺς ἐν Βηθλέεμ καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ὁρίοις αὐτῆς ἀπὸ διετοῦς καὶ κατωτέρω, κατὰ τὸν χρόνον ὃν ἠκρίβωσεν παρὰ τῶν μάγων.
records.gloss: Then Herod having seen that he was mocked by the magi was enraged exceedingly, and having sent he killed all the boys the [ones] in Bethlehem and in all the regions of it from two-year-old and under, according to the time which he ascertained from the magi.
pieces: When Herod saw that the magi had made a fool of him, he was furious. He sent soldiers and killed all the boys in Bethlehem and the area around it who were two years old or younger, in keeping with the time he had found out from the magi.

L.16: Then Herod, seeing that he had been tricked by the magi, became extremely angry, and sending [men], he killed all the boys in Bethlehem and in all its region, from two years old and under, according to the time that he had learned exactly from the magi.

R.16: Herod saw that the wise men had tricked him, and he became very angry. He sent soldiers to Bethlehem and the countryside around it, and they killed all the little boys there who were two years old or younger. Herod chose that age because of what the wise men had told him about when the star appeared.

decisions.choice: tricked: made a fool of, as Herod saw it
decisions.reason: The verb means to mock or make sport of. The magi did not mock Herod; they obeyed a warning from God (2:12). Matthew tells it as Herod saw it.

decisions.choice: the boys of Bethlehem: a small village, so perhaps a few dozen children at most
decisions.reason: Bethlehem was a village. The killing is not recorded outside Matthew, but it fits what is known of Herod, who had three of his own sons put to death.

decisions.choice: an echo of Pharaoh's order to kill the Hebrew boys (Exodus 1:22)
decisions.reason: As in 2:13, Herod acts like the Pharaoh of the exodus, and the child escapes as Moses did.

decisions.choice: two years and under, by the time he had learned: a margin around the star's appearing
decisions.reason: Herod sets the age from what the magi told him (2:7), and allows enough to be sure.

decisions.choice: wise men
decisions.reason: "Magi" is unfamiliar to new readers; Readable calls them wise men, and in 2:1 says that they studied the stars.

decisions.choice: sending [men] (L); he sent soldiers (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek "having sent, he killed" means he gave orders that others carried out. Literal brackets the men; Balanced and Readable say they were soldiers, as such men would have been.

records.heading: Herod kills the boys of Bethlehem

records.source: τότε ἐπληρώθη τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἰερεμίου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
records.gloss: Then was fulfilled the [thing] spoken through Jeremiah the prophet saying:
pieces: Then the word spoken through the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled:

L.17: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying:

R.17: This made what the prophet Jeremiah had said come true. He said:

decisions.choice: then was fulfilled: not "so that it might be fulfilled"
alternatives: the killing happened in order to fulfill Scripture
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Matthew writes "so that ... might be fulfilled" (1:22; 2:15, 23). Here, of Herod's crime, he writes only "then", and he does not say "by the Lord". The evil is Herod's; Scripture had already spoken of such grief.

records.source: Φωνὴ ἐν Ῥαμὰ ἠκούσθη, κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὀδυρμὸς πολύς· Ῥαχὴλ κλαίουσα τὰ τέκνα αὐτῆς, καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν παρακληθῆναι ὅτι οὐκ εἰσίν.
records.gloss: A voice in Ramah was heard, weeping and mourning great; Rachel weeping [for] the children of her, and not she would be comforted, because they are not.
pieces: "A sound was heard in Ramah, weeping and loud wailing: Rachel crying for her children and refusing all comfort, because they are gone."

L.18: "A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping [for] her children, and she would not be comforted, because they are not."

R.18: "People heard a loud sound in the town of Ramah. It was the sound of crying and great sadness. Rachel was crying for her children. She would not let anyone comfort her, because her children were gone."

decisions.choice: Jeremiah 31:15: Rachel weeping for her children taken into exile
alternatives: a prediction of the killing at Bethlehem only
decisions.reason: Rachel, Jacob's wife, was the mother of Joseph and Benjamin. Jeremiah pictures her weeping at Ramah, north of Jerusalem, as her descendants are led away to exile. The next verses promise that they will come back (Jeremiah 31:16-17). Matthew hears the same grief in Bethlehem, and the hope comes with Jesus.

decisions.choice: Ramah and Rachel: Rachel's grave was remembered on the way to Bethlehem
decisions.reason: Genesis 35:19 says Rachel was buried on the way to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem. Ramah was a town about five miles north of Jerusalem, where exiles were gathered (Jeremiah 40:1).

decisions.choice: they are not: they are dead
alternatives: they are absent for a time
decisions.reason: "They are not" is a way of saying that someone has died (Genesis 42:13, 36).

decisions.choice: they are gone (B); her children were gone (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plain words for the idiom.

records.source: Τελευτήσαντος δὲ τοῦ Ἡρῴδου ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος κυρίου φαίνεται κατ’ ὄναρ τῷ Ἰωσὴφ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ λέγων· Ἐγερθεὶς παράλαβε τὸ παιδίον καὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ πορεύου εἰς γῆν Ἰσραήλ, τεθνήκασιν γὰρ οἱ ζητοῦντες τὴν ψυχὴν τοῦ παιδίου.
records.gloss: Having died then the Herod, behold, an angel of Lord appears in a dream to the Joseph in Egypt \v 20 saying, Having arisen take the child and the mother of him and go into land of Israel, they have died for the [ones] seeking the life of the child.
pieces: After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt
and said, "Get up, take the child and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother, and go back to the land of Israel, because those who wanted the child dead have died."

L.19: And when Herod had died, look, an angel of [the] Lord appears in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
L.20: saying, "Get up, take the child and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother and go to [the] land of Israel, for those who were seeking the child's life have died."

R.19: Then Herod died. While Joseph was still in Egypt, an angel of the Lord came to him in a dream.
R.20: The angel said, "Get up! Take the child and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother and go back to the land of Israel. The people who were trying to kill the child are dead now."

decisions.choice: those who were seeking the child's life have died: the words God spoke to Moses
decisions.reason: In Exodus 4:19 God tells Moses to return to Egypt, "for all the men who were seeking your life have died". The plural fits Moses's story as much as Herod's.

decisions.choice: Herod's death: in 4 BC
decisions.reason: Herod the Great died in 4 BC, and his kingdom was divided among three of his sons (see 2:22).

decisions.choice: the land of Israel: the land God promised to his people
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls the promised land, not one province. The family later settles in Galilee (2:22).

decisions.choice: appears (L); appeared (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:13, Literal keeps the present tense of the Greek.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this word to point to what comes next. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal uses "look", and Balanced and Readable carry its force in the flow of the sentence, as in 1:20.

records.heading: The return to Nazareth

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἐγερθεὶς παρέλαβε τὸ παιδίον καὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς γῆν Ἰσραήλ.
records.gloss: He then having arisen took the child and the mother of him and entered into land of Israel.
pieces: Joseph got up, took the child and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother, and went into the land of Israel.

L.21: So he got up and took the child and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother and went into [the] land of Israel.

R.21: So Joseph got up. He took the child and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother and went back to the land of Israel.

decisions.choice: got up and took: obedience in the words of the command
decisions.reason: The narrative repeats the angel's words (2:20), as 1:24 and 2:14 do. Joseph does just what he is told.

decisions.choice: Joseph
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Joseph at the start of the sentence.

records.source: ἀκούσας δὲ ὅτι Ἀρχέλαος βασιλεύει τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἀντὶ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ Ἡρῴδου ἐφοβήθη ἐκεῖ ἀπελθεῖν· χρηματισθεὶς δὲ κατ’ ὄναρ ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὰ μέρη τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἐλθὼν κατῴκησεν εἰς πόλιν λεγομένην Ναζαρέτ, ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τῶν προφητῶν ὅτι Ναζωραῖος κληθήσεται.
records.gloss: Having heard then that Archelaus reigns over the Judea in place of the father of him Herod he was afraid there to go; having been warned then in a dream he withdrew into the parts of the Galilee, \v 23 and having come he settled in a town being called Nazareth, so that might be fulfilled the [thing] spoken through the prophets that Nazarene he will be called.
pieces: But when he heard that Archelaus had succeeded his father Herod as ruler of Judea, he was afraid to go there. Warned in a dream, he went instead to the region of Galilee
and made his home in a town called Nazareth. This was so that what the prophets had said would be fulfilled, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would be called a Nazarene.

L.22: But hearing that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there, and having been warned in a dream, he withdrew to the parts of Galilee,
L.23: and coming [there], he settled in a town called Nazareth, so that what was spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be called a Nazarene.

R.22: But Joseph heard that Archelaus had become the ruler of Judea after his father Herod. So Joseph was afraid to go there. God warned him in a dream, and he went to the area of Galilee instead.
R.23: He went to live in a town called Nazareth. This made what the prophets had said come true: people would call {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a Nazarene, someone from Nazareth.

decisions.choice: Archelaus: Herod's son, who ruled Judea from 4 BC to AD 6
alternatives: a king with Herod's full title
decisions.reason: At Herod's death Rome gave Archelaus Judea, Samaria and Idumea, but not the title of king; Galilee went to his brother Herod Antipas. Archelaus ruled harshly, and Rome removed him in AD 6. "Reigns" is used loosely of his rule.

decisions.choice: Nazarene: a man from Nazareth, perhaps with a play on a prophetic word
alternatives: a Nazirite, one under a vow (Numbers 6)
a play on the Hebrew word for "branch" in Isaiah 11:1
decisions.reason: No verse of the Old Testament says "he will be called a Nazarene". The word means "from Nazareth". Many read a play on the Hebrew word for the "branch" from Jesse's root (Isaiah 11:1), or on the Nazirite of Judges 13:5. Others see the prophets' picture of a despised servant, since Nazareth was an obscure village (John 1:46).

decisions.choice: through the prophets: a theme of the prophets, not one quotation
decisions.reason: Only here does Matthew say "the prophets" in the plural and introduce the words with "that" rather than "saying". He sums up what several prophets said.

decisions.choice: warned: given a warning by God
decisions.reason: As in 2:12, the warning comes from God.

decisions.choice: had succeeded his father Herod as ruler (B); had become the ruler (R)
decisions.reason: Archelaus did not hold the title of king, so Balanced and Readable say "ruler".

decisions.choice: God warned him; someone from Nazareth
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the passive implies, and says what "Nazarene" means.
